title: WHERE ARE YOU?
paragraphs:
WHERE ARE YOU?
The First Question God Asked
There are questions that gather information.
And then there are questions that expose souls.
The first question God ever asked in Scripture belongs to the second category.
It was not asked because God lacked knowledge.
It was asked because humanity had lost itself.

The question echoes across every generation, every city, every church pew, every hidden addiction, every broken marriage, every wandering heart, every sleepless night, every carefully curated social media profile, every secret shame, every silent tear.
A question so ancient that it was spoken in the Garden of Eden.
A question so current that it may be speaking directly to you right now.
Genesis paints a world untouched by death, untouched by corruption, untouched by betrayal. Humanity was not merely alive; humanity was in communion with God.
Adam and Eve walked with Him.
The Hebrew language captures something beautiful in Genesis 3:8:

וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ אֶת־קוֹל יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים
(Vayyishme'u et-qol YHWH Elohim)
"And they heard the voice of the LORD God..."
The Hebrew word qol (קוֹל) means voice, sound, thunder, or audible presence. God was not a distant concept. He was not an abstract force. He was present.
The serpent whispered the oldest lie ever told:
Instead, it became humanity's greatest tragedy.
The moment Adam and Eve ate the forbidden fruit, something shattered.
For the first time, they experienced guilt.
For the first time, they experienced shame.
For the first time, they experienced fear.
The same fear that still haunts humanity today.
The fear of being fully known.
The fear that if God saw everything, He would turn away.
And so they did what sinners have been doing ever since.
Genesis 3:8 says they hid themselves among the trees of the garden.
The creatures attempted to hide from their Creator.
Dust attempted to disappear from the One who formed it.
The finite attempted to escape the Infinite.
Yet before we laugh at Adam and Eve, we should recognize ourselves.
Many people know about God while desperately hiding from Him.

וַיִּקְרָא יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים אֶל־הָאָדָם וַיֹּאמֶר לוֹ אַיֶּכָּה
(Vayiqra YHWH Elohim el-ha'adam vayomer lo ayekah)
"But the LORD God called to the man and said to him, 'Where are you?'"
This is not a geographical question.
The omniscient Creator did not suddenly lose track of His creation.
Adam knew where he was physically.
He no longer knew where he stood relationally.
This is one of the most overlooked displays of grace in the entire Bible.
Notice who takes the first step.
The Gospel begins long before Bethlehem.
The Gospel begins in a garden where a holy God comes searching for guilty people.
The first question God asks reveals the heart of redemption itself.
The God who moves toward sinners.
The entire Bible unfolds from this reality.
"For the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost."
The mission of Christ was not merely to teach.
Not merely to provide moral guidance.
The same God who walked through Eden asking, "Where are you?" entered history in flesh and blood to find those who could not find their way back.
Every page of Scripture points toward this pursuit.
Abraham was not searching for God when God called him.
Moses was not searching for God when the bush burned.
David was not searching for God when Samuel arrived.
Paul was not searching for Jesus on the Damascus Road.
The sheep do not rescue themselves.
This is why the Gospel is fundamentally different from every system of human effort.
Religion says, "Find your way to God."
The Gospel says, "God came looking for you."
The scandal of grace is that God pursues people who deserve judgment.
The greatest surprise in Genesis 3 is not that Adam sinned.
It is that God came searching.
Because if justice alone had spoken, the story would have ended there.
Yet mercy stepped into the garden.
And mercy still walks through gardens.
Maybe you are far from God.
Maybe your faith has become mechanical.
Maybe your prayer life has become silent.
Maybe you've hidden behind years of pretending.
Maybe you're exhausted from carrying secrets.
Maybe you're tired of performing righteousness while feeling spiritually empty.
Maybe you're sitting in church physically present but emotionally distant.
Maybe you know exactly where Adam was.
Trying to manage your own exposure.
The beauty of Genesis is that God does not begin with condemnation.
God invites Adam to step out of hiding.
Because the opposite of intimacy is not hatred.
The enemy's strategy has never changed.
Then convince them they are too far gone.
But the Gospel destroys that lie.
At Calvary, Jesus carried every sin that makes us hide.
Isaiah 53 says He bore our iniquities.
The Hebrew word used throughout the passage carries the idea of carrying a crushing burden.
Christ carried what was crushing us.
He took our guilt so we could receive His righteousness.
He took our shame so we could stand forgiven.
He took our death so we could receive life.
This is why the story moves from a garden to a cross.
In Eden, humanity hid among trees.
At Calvary, salvation hung on one.
The last Adam, Jesus Christ, brought reconciliation.
The story that began with hiding ends with open access to God through Christ.
And perhaps that is why Genesis 3 continues to resonate so deeply.
Because every human heart knows the experience of hiding.
But every human heart was also created to be found.
The question God asked Adam is still moving through history.
It is moving through this article.
It is moving through your screen.
It is moving through your conscience.
Not because God does not know where you are.
But because He wants you to know where you are.
And more importantly, He wants you to know where He is.
The Gospel is not the story of humanity finding God.
It is the story of God finding humanity.
Your testimony may become someone else's turning point.
Because the greatest miracle was never that Adam finally found God.
The greatest miracle is that God came looking for Adam.
And He is still looking for us.
The God who asked, "Where are you?" already knew the answer.
He asked because love was calling hidden people back into the light.
